root_cause.text: io_uring's io_zcrx_map_area() relied on area->is_mapped to drive sgtable cleanup, but io_populate_area_dma() can fail after page_sg_table has already been initialized and before is_mapped is set, leaving the non-dmabuf sgtable leaked on the error path.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that when io_populate_area_dma() fails, "io_zcrx_map_area() will have an initialised and not freed table" and that cleanup was skipped because "!is_mapped prevents that"; the patch adds an explicit dma_unmap_sgtable(ifq->dev, &area->mem.page_sg_table, ...) when ret is nonzero and !area->mem.is_dmabuf, before setting area->is_mapped only on success.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that when io_populate_area_dma() fails, "io_zcrx_map_area() will have an initialised and not freed table" and that cleanup was skipped because "!is_mapped prevents that"; the patch adds an explicit dma_unmap_sgtable(ifq->dev, &area->mem.page_sg_table, ...) when ret is nonzero and !area->mem.is_dmabuf, before setting area->is_mapped only on success.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unmap non-dmabuf DMA mappings when io_populate_area_dma() fails to fix an error-path DMA mapping leak.
intent_record.what: After calling io_populate_area_dma(ifq, area), the code now checks whether ret is nonzero and area->mem.is_dmabuf is false, and in that case calls dma_unmap_sgtable(ifq->dev, &area->mem.page_sg_table, DMA_FROM_DEVICE, IO_DMA_ATTR) before continuing; the existing logic that sets area->is_mapped = true only when ret == 0 remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: If DMA population fails for a non-dmabuf-backed area, the newly added unmap call releases the previously mapped scatter-gather table instead of leaving it mapped, preventing leaked or stale DMA mappings on the error path while preserving existing behavior for dmabuf-backed memory and successful mappings.

grouping_result.intent: Unmap non-dmabuf DMA mappings when io_populate_area_dma() fails to fix an error-path DMA mapping leak.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the described root cause by cleaning up non-dmabuf DMA/sgtable state on the io_populate_area_dma() failure path, addressing the leak that occurs before is_mapped is set.

candidates.rationale: This conditional delays setting area->is_mapped until after io_populate_area_dma() fully succeeds. If io_populate_area_dma() partially initializes page_sg_table and then fails, cleanup logic driven by is_mapped will not run, causing the sgtable leak.

The mapping state flag is only set on full success, but cleanup later relies on this flag to decide whether to unmap/free the non-dmabuf sgtable. Partial initialization before this assignment leaves resources allocated yet marked unmapped.

This call can partially initialize DMA mapping state, including page_sg_table, before returning an error. Because subsequent cleanup depends on area->is_mapped instead of actual partial initialization, this call site is directly involved in exposing the leak on the error path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement sets the mapping-state flag only after io_populate_area_dma() returns full success. Because error cleanup was driven by area->is_mapped, any partial initialization of page_sg_table done before a failing return left resources allocated but not marked mapped, causing the non-dmabuf sgtable leak.

This conditional gates the area->is_mapped update on complete success. That means partial DMA setup performed by io_populate_area_dma() on an error return is invisible to later cleanup logic that relies on is_mapped, enabling the leak.

This call can partially initialize DMA mapping state, including page_sg_table, before failing. Since the surrounding logic did not mark the area mapped until after full success, the resources created by this call could be leaked on the error path.

Author: Pavel Begunkov <asml.silence@gmail.com>

    io_uring/zcrx: return error from io_zcrx_map_area_*
    
    io_zcrx_map_area_*() helpers return the number of processed niovs, which
    we use to unroll some of the mappings for user memory areas. It's
    unhandy, and dmabuf doesn't care about it. Return an error code instead

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown diff is sufficient because it includes the relevant error-handling logic in both `io_zcrx_map_area_umem()` and `io_zcrx_map_area()`. The root cause was that cleanup depended on `area->is_mapped`, while `io_populate_area_dma()` could fail after sgtable initialization but before `area->is_mapped` was set, leaking the non-dmabuf sgtable on the error path. In this commit, the user-memory path now performs partial cleanup inside `io_zcrx_map_area_umem()` itself: `if (i != area->nia.num_niovs) { __io_zcrx_unmap_area(ifq, area, i); return -EINVAL; }`. That means unmapping/cleanup happens before returning failure, without relying on `area->is_mapped` being set. Also, `io_zcrx_map_area()` now only sets `area->is_mapped = true` when `ret == 0`, and otherwise simply returns the error: `if (ret == 0) area->is_mapped = true; return ret;`. This is consistent with the fix described in the commit message: moving failure partial unmapping into `io_zcrx_map_area_umem()`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is no longer present in this version.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full new map/unmap/error-path logic for the area. The reported root cause is specifically about cleanup being driven by `area->is_mapped` while a partially initialized mapping state may exist before `is_mapped` is set, causing a leak on error. In this commit, `io_zcrx_map_area()` performs per-page DMA mapping in a loop and, on partial failure, explicitly cleans up the already-mapped subset before returning: `if (i != area->nia.num_niovs) { __io_zcrx_unmap_area(ifq, area, i); return -EINVAL; }`. Only after full success does it set `area->is_mapped = true;`. Therefore, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present here for this function: the error path does not rely on `area->is_mapped` for cleanup of partially established state. However, the fix described in the root cause is also not shown here because this code is about DMA page mapping/unmapping, not sgtable/page_sg_table cleanup, and `io_zcrx_unmap_area()` still gates normal teardown on `if (area->is_mapped)`. Since the specific sgtable cleanup fix is absent from this function body, `is_fixed` is false.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full relevant error-handling and cleanup interaction between mapping and release. The root cause was that cleanup 'relied on area->is_mapped to drive sgtable cleanup' while 'io_populate_area_dma() can fail after page_sg_table has already been initialized and before is_mapped is set', leaking the non-dmabuf sgtable. In this commit, the fix is present because UMEM areas now store the active sg table in `mem->sgt` before mapping: `mem->sgt = &mem->page_sg_table;` in `io_import_umem()`. Cleanup no longer hardcodes `page_sg_table` or depends on `is_mapped`; instead `io_release_area_mem()` does `sg_free_table(mem->sgt);` and then `mem->sgt = NULL;`. Also `io_populate_area_dma()` now derives the sg table from `area->mem.sgt` via `struct sg_table *sgt = area->mem.sgt;`, and `io_zcrx_map_area()` no longer passes a separate local sgtable pointer. Since the sg table pointer is established for umem areas before `io_populate_area_dma()` runs, the initialized sgtable can be found and freed even if mapping fails before `area->is_mapped = true;`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent in this version, and the fix is already included.
